title: Exponential online mistakes at every width after arbitrarily small Gaussian anisotropy
status: Conventional proofs with independent AI-agent mathematical reviews; not Lean formalized.
review_scope: Two independent final-source reviews checked all nonlinear competitors at every width, exact two-sided and cyclic-block calibration, the projection-fiber count, measure compactness/equality, every explicit quantitative constant, the actual Gaussian posterior, common mean-field scale, IID upper bound, gamma convention, and theorem/proof correspondence. Both reviews identify the exact final source hash; no mathematical correction was required.
visual_check: Rendered final PDF pages 1, 7, 13, and 15 were inspected: alphabetical authors and footnote, explicit linear-calibration theorem and measure model, quantitative appendix equations, and references. No clipping or malformed mathematics observed.

author_check.exact_footnote: Authors are listed in alphabetical order.
author_check.pdf_author_metadata: ChatGPT-6 Astra; Kaarel Hanni; Dmitry Vaintrob

critical_scope: Fixed standard tanh, one hidden layer, augmented constant input, full Boolean cube, strict global output margin greater than 1/2, exact labels, and every finite width N>=1.
The prior has positive coordinate anisotropy lambda_i=1+delta*2^(-i); this does not settle exact isotropy.
Ordinary majority has bounded-weight teacher complexity C_2=1 and Boolean circuit size Theta(d).
For odd d>=17, every fixed delta in (0,1) gives at least 2^floor(d/8) designated mistakes after a large calibration prefix.
For odd q>=3 and d=9q, exactly 2q cyclic calibration inputs give exactly 9^((q+1)/2) designated mistake rounds for every 0<delta<=1/(80000q^3).
Canonical sigma scale may depend on width. One sufficiently small positive mean-field scale t=sqrt(N)*sigma works at every width.

For each fixed gamma>1, unit prefactor gives the conclusions at every sufficiently large width. One sufficiently small common prefactor works for all widths and all gamma>=1. Unit-prefactor gamma=1 is not covered.
The same priors and target have IID sample bound O((d^4+log(1/beta))/rho), with the small mean-field scale uniform over widths and all target-consistent histories.
At exact isotropy the candidate tier has equal function masses and logarithmic expected sampling errors until that tier is exhausted; no global isotropic online upper bound is claimed.
